blocks.name: All Subplans : Global Studies General Requirement

rules.name: Globally Focused Core Course
rules.desc:
All students must complete 28 units, including one globally-focused core course (typically 3–5 units) that centers their subplan work in a larger global context.
First-year students should plan to take COLLEGE 119: Making of the Modern World, which fulfills both the Global Studies minor and COLLEGE global perspectives requirements.
Those students unable to take COLLEGE 119 should, in consultation with their subplan advisor, select a replacement course from the pre-approved courses below that draw from a wide range of academic disciplines. Students should be advised that the pre-approved courses may change from year to year and should consult their subplan advisor for the most current list and any prerequisites. Students are encouraged to take their globally-focused core course early in their career. If a student wishes to use a course not on the pre-approved list, they may also petition to do so by contacting their subplan advisor.
The remaining units are unique to each specialization, and students participating in the Bing Overseas Studies Program are especially encouraged to enroll.

rules.name: Minor in Global Studies with African Studies Specialization
rules.desc:
The Global Studies minor, African Studies specialization, offers students the opportunity to complement their primary course of study with an in-depth, interdisciplinary exploration of Africa's cultures, histories, politics, religions, and societies. Students from any major interested in applying for admission to this minor program should consult the minor advisor at the Center for African Studies. Students declare the minor and the African Studies specialization in Axess (see below for detailed instructions). Students should consult with their minor advisor to develop individual programs. The minor is especially well-suited for undergraduates who plan to do service, research, or study abroad in Africa as part of their Stanford experience.
To declare the Global Studies minor with an African Studies specialization, students must set an appointment with the Associate Director of the Center for African Studies, Robin Chapdelaine, then declare the minor and subplan in Axess.

rules.name: Learning Outcomes
rules.desc: The Global Studies minor specialization in African Studies enables students to develop critical knowledge and skills, organize their interest in Africa into a coherent course of study through directed mentorship and participation in the intellectual community, and prepare for research, study, or service in Africa. Upon completion of the requirements, the Center for African Studies makes the final certification of the minor. The minor and the specialization appear on the transcript but not on the diploma.

rules.name: Requirements
rules.desc: Please note that students are required to complete a total of 25 Units combined through the requirements listed below.

children.name: Entry-Level Course Requirement
children.desc: One entry-level course that covers more than one region of Africa.
children.notes: Students may not double-count courses to complete major and minor requirements. Coursework must be letter-graded, except where letter grades are not offered.

children.name: Sub-Saharan African Language Requirement
children.desc: At least one quarter’s exposure to a sub-Saharan African language. The Center for African Studies and the Special Languages Program of the Language Center can arrange instruction in several languages spoken in West, East, Central, and Southern Africa.

children.name: Focus of Study Requirement
children.desc: A designated focus of study, either disciplinary or regional, through a three-course concentration developed with the minor advisor.

children.name: Capstone (optional)
children.desc:
Students may work with the subplan advisor to develop a capstone project to count towards the unit fulfillment of the minor. Projects may include (but are not limited to):
1. Research with units through directed reading under the supervision of the subplan advisor.
Research may take place at Stanford or during a relevant study abroad program, and options may include regional fieldwork, creative arts projects, short films, etc.​​
2. Advanced language study beyond the subplan minimum requirement with units through directed reading under the supervision of the subplan advisor.
Intensive language training may take place at Stanford, off-campus, or overseas.
Students may propose other projects related to their subplan.

rules.name: Subplan: European Studies
rules.desc:
Minor in Global Studies with European Studies Specialization:
The Stanford Global Studies minor, European Studies specialization, is designed for undergraduates with an interdisciplinary interest in the history, culture, politics, societies, and institutions of Europe, past and present. The minor is especially well-suited for undergraduates who plan to make Europe-based overseas studies a part of their Stanford experience, as those courses fulfill the requirements for the minor.
To declare the Global Studies minor with a European Studies specialization, students must set an appointment with minor advisors, Anna Grzymala-Busse, Faculty Director, or Christophe Crombez, then declare the minor and subplan in Axess.

rules.name: Learning Outcomes
rules.desc: The Global Studies minor specialization in European Studies enables students to: Organize their studies in a coherent and mentored minor. Prepare for or follow up on involvement in a Bing Overseas Studies Program in Europe. Upon completion of the requirements, the final certification of the minor is made by Stanford Global Studies. The minor and the specialization appear on the transcript but not on the diploma.

children.name: Required Survey Course (5 units) on European History or Culture
children.desc: Complete at least 1 of the following courses or another similar course approved by the advisor.

children.name: Electives
children.desc: Earn at least 15 credits from the following courses or other similar courses approved by the advisor.
children.notes:
• The above 15 units should be on a coherent theme of interest developed with the minor advisor. This combination of courses can be on any thematic subject with an interdisciplinary and comparative focus on Europe.

• At least 13 of the 28 units must be completed on the Stanford campus.

• Coursework must be letter-graded work, except where letter grades are not offered.

children.name: Modern European Language Proficiency
children.desc:
Advanced proficiency in a modern European language achieved by one of the following: Completion of six quarters of college-level study of a modern European language. Completion of a course taught in a modern European language at the 100-level or higher and with a letter grade of B or higher. This may be a course on a European language, literature, or other subject if it fulfills the above criteria. (This course may satisfy both the minor foreign language requirement and the minor 28-unit minimum requirement.)
Achieve the advanced proficiency level on the ACTFL scale in a test administered by the Stanford Language Center.

children.name: Capstone (optional)
children.desc:
Students may work with the subplan advisor to develop a capstone project to count towards the unit fulfillment of the minor. Projects may include (but are not limited to):
1. Research with units through directed reading under the supervision of the subplan advisor.
Research may take place at Stanford or during a relevant study abroad program, and options may include regional fieldwork, creative arts projects, short films, etc.​​
2. Advanced language study beyond the subplan minimum requirement with units through directed reading under the supervision of the subplan advisor.
Intensive language training may take place at Stanford, off-campus, or overseas.
Students may propose other projects related to their subplan.

rules.name: Subplan: Iranian Studies
rules.desc:
Minor in Global Studies with Iranian Studies Specialization:
The Stanford Global Studies minor, Iranian Studies specialization, is designed for undergraduates with an interdisciplinary interest in the modern history and politics of Iran or the Middle East; Islam, particularly Shiism; the geopolitics of the Middle East; and the relevant religions, ethnicities, and cultures.
Students consult with their minor advisor to develop individual programs. The minor is especially well-suited for undergraduates planning graduate studies, teaching, or research and analysis focused on Iran.
Upon completion of the requirements, the final certification of the minor is made by Stanford Global Studies. The minor and the specialization appear on the transcript but not on the diploma.
To declare the Global Studies minor with an Iranian Studies specialization, students must set an appointment with the Associate Director for the Iranian Studies Program, Roma Parhad, then declare the minor and subplan in Axess.

rules.name: Learning Outcomes
rules.desc:
The Global Studies minor specialization in Iranian Studies enables students to:
1. Develop critical knowledge and skills in Iranian Studies.
2. Organize their interest in Iranian Studies into a coherent course of study through directed mentorship and participation in an intellectual community.
3. Enhance students’ understanding and participation in an increasingly global world.
Upon completion of the requirements, the final certification of the minor is made by the Iranian Studies Program. The minor and the specialization appear on the transcript but not on the diploma.

children.name: Area Course Requirement
children.desc:
One area or region-specific entry-level course on Iran and the Middle East. Consent by the Faculty Director of Iranian Studies is required by petition for alternate area course not included in the list below.
At least 3-5 units must be from the list of area courses.

• Coursework must be taken for a letter-grade, except where letter grades are not offered.

• Students may not double-count courses to complete major and minor requirements.
Other courses may also fulfill the requirements. Students should consult their Iranian Studies minor advisor concerning which courses might satisfy minor requirements.

children.name: Persian Language Requirement
children.desc:
Complete two quarters of Persian Language courses, or proven Persian Language proficiency.
Up to 15 units of language courses may be applied toward the minor.

children.name: Core Course Requirement

rules.name: Elective Course Requirement

• Coursework must be letter-graded work, except where letter grades are not offered.

Other courses may also fulfill this requirement. Students should consult their Iranian Studies minor advisor concerning which courses might satisfy minor requirements.

rules.name: Subplan: Islamic Studies
rules.desc:
The minor in Global Studies with specialization in Islamic Studies offers students an interdisciplinary and global exploration of Islam and Islamicate societies and cultures. The focus is on knowledge of Islam in all its internal complexity, the history of Islam from its beginnings to the 21st century, Islamicate social contexts, and the diversity of human experience as seen in literature and the arts originating in societies affected by Islamic civilizations. Students explore the global extent of Islam and the growth of its diasporas by taking courses on geographical regions such as the Middle East, South Asia, Eurasia, Africa, Western Europe, and the Americas and from disciplines such as anthropology, art and art history, comparative literature, history, political science, international relations, and religious studies.
Students consult with their minor advisor to develop individual programs.
To declare the Global Studies minor with an Islamic Studies specialization, students must set an appointment with the Associate Director for the Islamic Studies Program, Dr. Halil Yenigun, then declare the minor and subplan in Axess.

rules.name: Learning Outcomes
rules.desc:
The Global Studies minor specialization in Islamic Studies enables students to:

• Recognize, explain, and analyze the beliefs, ideas, practices, histories, ethics, intellectual traditions, cultural and artistic expressions, and politics in Muslim-majority and Muslim minority contexts, including non-Muslim communities.

• Apply theoretical concepts, social scientific, or interpretive methods from the humanities and social sciences to design and construct independent research or arguments on any aspect of Islam, Muslims, or non-Muslims in Muslim-majority settings that will prepare them for further pursuit of an advanced degree.

• Demonstrate at least an elementary level of proficiency in speaking, comprehending, and writing in one of the native languages spoken in Muslim-majority countries.
Upon completion of the requirements, the final certification of the minor is made by the Abbasi Program in Islamic Studies. The minor and the specialization appear on the transcript but not on the diploma.

children.name: Area Specific/Islamic Studies Entry Course Requirement
children.desc: At least one course must be an area-specific entry course focusing on the Islamic world. These courses may be used to fulfill this requirement.

children.name: Islamic Studies Core Elective Courses
children.desc:
A minimum of 25 units of Islamic studies-related courses. Coursework must be letter-graded, except where letter grades are not offered.
At least one course must be from each of the following areas:

• Islam: Religion, Arts, Literatures, and Cultures

• Islam in History

• Islam and Politics

rules.name: Subplan: Latin American Studies
rules.desc: The Global Studies minor, Latin American Studies (GS-LAS) specialization, consists of courses surveying the Latin American region’s interdisciplinary fields, including the humanities, social sciences, and environmental and health studies through in-depth coursework and language training. We welcome students from all majors. Those interested in declaring the GS-LAS minor must develop an individual program plan and set up an appointment with a GS-LAS minor advisor (either the CLAS Academic and Student Services Officer or the Associate Director) to review their minor plan PRIOR to declaring in Axess. Units taken for major credit cannot be double-counted towards the minor. The GS-LAS minor is especially well-suited for undergraduates who plan to make service, research, or study abroad in Latin America a part of their Stanford experience. The minor and the specialization appear on the transcript but not on the diploma.

rules.name: Learning outcomes
rules.desc:
The Global Studies minor specialization in Latin American Studies enables students to:

• Engage in the integrated understanding of the region’s interdisciplinary fields, including the humanities, social sciences, and environmental and health studies

• Gain a conceptual foundation to pursue a variety of career paths in the public and private sectors pertaining to the region

• Acquire language and cultural competency

rules.name: Core requirements
rules.desc: At least 15 of the 28 units must be completed at Stanford. All courses counted toward the minor must be taken for a letter grade, except where letter grades are not offered.
rules.notes: Note: Some courses may have prerequisites or special enrollment requirements. Students are responsible for completing any prerequisites and/or securing an instructor’s permission to enroll, as needed.

children.name: Introductory course requirement
children.desc: Introductory course must be taken for 5 units. A substitute introductory course for ILAC 131 may be approved by petition.

rules.name: Theoretical or geographic area course requirement
rules.desc:
At least 14 units in courses comprising a coherent area focus on a theoretical problem or regional issue in the fields of humanities, social sciences, and/or environment and health.
Listed courses are subject to availability. If a course in question is not listed here, please contact CLAS Academic Services by the first week of the quarter to inquire about the petition process.

rules.name: Foreign language requirement
rules.desc: Completion of three quarters, or equivalent, of college-level study of a language spoken in Latin America or achieving intermediate level of proficiency in a language spoken in Latin America on the ACTFL scale in a test administered by the Stanford Language Center. If completion of the three-quarter sequence of language training is done at Stanford University, students may apply up to six units towards the 28-unit minimum requirement. Contact the Stanford Language Center for test dates and procedures.

2. Advanced language study beyond the subplan minimum requirement with units through directed reading under the supervision of the subplan advisor.

blocks.name: Subplan: Russian, East European, and Eurasian Studies

rules.name: Subplan: Russian, East European, and Eurasian Studies
rules.desc:
The Stanford Global Studies minor, Russian, East European and Eurasian Studies specialization, is designed for undergraduates with an interdisciplinary interest in the history, politics, culture, and institutions of the REEES region or particular areas within it.
To declare the Global Studies minor with a Russian, East European and Eurasian Studies specialization, students must set an appointment with minor advisors Karla Oeler, CREEES Faculty Director, or Jovana Lazić, CREEES Associate Director, then declare the minor and subplan in Axess.

rules.name: Learning Outcomes
rules.desc:
The Global Studies minor specialization in Russian, East European and Eurasian Studies enables students to:

• Develop essential skills and literacy in Russian, East European and Eurasian Studies

• Acquire valuable training in a language of Central Europe; Eastern Europe; or Eurasia

• Prepare for graduate study, and/or a career in the public or private sector for which competency in Russian, East European and Eurasian Studies is required or advantageous

children.name: Language Proficiency Requirement
children.desc:
0-10 units: Proficiency Requirement in a Language of either Central Europe; Eastern Europe; or Eurasia.
May be satisfied by any of the following:

• A one-year sequence at any level, or its equivalent (e.g. RUSSLANG 1A+2A)

• Intermediate-High level Russian language proficiency on the ACTFL OPI

• To inquire about demonstrating proficiency in other area languages, consult with the CREEES Faculty Director or Associate Director.

• An accredited intensive summer language program may be considered in consultation with the CREEES Faculty Director or Associate Director.

children.name: REEES Core Courses
children.desc:
≥ 12 units: Core Courses (from pre-approved list)

• Core courses must be spread across at least 2, ideally 3, disciplines

• Additional courses may be considered in consultation with the CREEES Faculty Director or Associate Director

children.name: REEES Current Issues Courses (optional)
children.desc: A maximum of 3 units may be counted towards the 28-unit total

2. Advanced language study beyond the subplan minimum requirement with units through directed reading under the supervision of the subplan advisor.

rules.name: Subplan: South Asian Studies
rules.desc:
The Global Studies minor, South Asian Studies specialization, offers students a focused study from an interdisciplinary perspective of the cultures, histories, politics, religions, and societies of South Asia, including Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. The Global Studies Minor with Specialization in South Asian Studies is open to students in any major. Students consult with their minor advisor to develop individual programs.
To declare the Global Studies minor with a South Asian Studies specialization, students must set an appointment with the Associate Director of the Center for South Asia, Lalita du Perron, then declare the minor and subplan in Axess.

rules.name: Learning Outcomes
rules.desc:
The Global Studies minor specialization in South Asian Studies enables students to:

• Acquire a nuanced and sophisticated understanding of the texts and contexts of South Asian Studies

• Work on this geographical and disciplinary area within the broader contours, conversations, and methods of Global Studies

• Enhance students’ ability to understand and participate in an increasingly global world

• Develop critical and wide-ranging insight into a key world area.

Upon completion of the requirements, the final certification of the minor is made by the Center for South Asian Studies. The minor and the specialization appear on the transcript but not on the diploma.

rules.name: Additional Course Requirements
rules.desc: At least 25 units of qualifying courses. Students may not double-count courses to complete major and minor requirements. At least 10 of the 25 units must be completed at Stanford. All courses counted toward the minor must be taken for a letter grade, except where letter grades are not offered. To view a more up-to-date course list, visit the program website.

children.name: South Asian Studies Introductory Course Requirement
Electives
children.notes:

• At least 10 of the 25 units must be completed at Stanford.

children.name: Foreign Language Requirement
children.desc:

Completion of two introductory language courses in a South Asian language such as Urdu, Hindi, Persian, Bengali, Pashto, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Gujarati, Malayalam, Garhwali, Nepalese, Tibetan, or Sindhi; other languages may also qualify.
Intermediate proficiency in any of the above languages, as measured by the ACTFL scale in a test administered by the Stanford Language Center.
A maximum of 15 language units, in a relevant language as described above, may be counted towards the total units required for the Global Minor, South Asia Subplan.
